direction: Maintain a diversity archive of distinct polished local optima and recombine them by geometric crossover. Generate 15–30 LP-polished optima from large kicks, cluster them by contact-graph hash and pairwise Procrustes RMSD after optimal $SO(8)$ alignment (Kabsch) and point matching (Hungarian assignment on the aligned dot matrix), and keep only representatives with RMSD $>0.05$ from those already archived. For two parents, align them, take the child’s points from parent A inside a random spherical cap or half-space and the matched complementary points from parent B, delete near-duplicates (cosine $>0.9$) and refill by farthest-point probing, then anneal and LP-polish; accept children into the archive if they are structurally novel even when $10^{-7}$–$10^{-5}$ worse, and use archive members—not only the incumbent—as parents in later rounds.

idea: Optimise few seeds under exact cyclic group invariance then release symmetry in stages with free quenches and LP polish.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained constructions from scratch, then release the symmetry in stages. For example use the order-7 rotation group generated by block-diagonal rotations through $2\pi/7,4\pi/7,6\pi/7$ in three coordinate planes (plus two fixed axes): a generic seed orbit has 7 points, so 24 seeds give exactly 168 points; optimise only the 24 seeds under exact group invariance with soft-max repulsion, also trying orbit-size factorizations $168=12\cdot14=8\cdot21=6\cdot28$ and E8-root subsets obtained by greedily deleting 72 of the 240 E8 minimal vectors to minimise pairs at cosine $1/2$. After convergence, release constraints in stages (seed-tied $\to$ orbit-cluster perturbations of amplitude $10^{-3},10^{-2},5\times10^{-2}$ $\to$ fully free points), quenching and LP-polishing at each stage, so the final code can inherit balanced contacts and near-equal degrees from the symmetric ansatz rather than from the record.

idea: Jointly delete the whole rattler-plus-hub stratum and re-solve it as a coupled subsystem with sequential deepest-hole reinsertion plus frozen-core boundary annealing before full thaw and LP polish.
direction: Delete and jointly re-solve the whole rattler-plus-hub stratum, not 1–4 points. Remove all $\sim$44 zero-contact points together with 8–16 randomly chosen overloaded points (degree $\ge8$) and their nearest neighbours (block sizes $k=32,48,64$ in different trials), freeze the remaining core, and reinsert the block sequentially from $50\,000$ random probes scored by maximum dot to the current set, then jointly anneal inserted points plus boundary points (core points having a dot $>0.3$ with any inserted point) while the deep core stays fixed for $1000$ steps before a full thaw and LP polish. This treats rattlers as a misplaced subsystem whose optimal positions depend on each other, which one-at-a-time void filling cannot capture.

idea: Step along floppy modes of the tangent rigidity matrix to change contact topology, then re-jam with soft-max annealing and LP squeeze.
direction: Make coordinated moves along rigidity/floppy modes of the near-contact graph instead of isotropic kicks. Build active pair sets at slack thresholds $10^{-7},10^{-5},10^{-4}$ (not just $10^{-9}$), form the tangent rigidity matrix for those pairs (rows in the $168\times7$ tangent coordinates), compute its smallest $\sim$50 singular vectors by randomized SVD, and step random combinations of them with total angular displacements $0.02$–$0.15$ rad, which preserve most contacts to first order while changing which pairs become tight. Follow each such step by soft-max annealing ($\beta:50\to600$, $1500$ steps) and short LP polish; keep the result only if its contact graph at slack $10^{-5}$ has Jaccard similarity $<0.9$ to the parent or its score improves, and iterate this as the main loop rather than single-point noise.

idea: Homotopy to successively lower target cosines with tangent-projected Gauss-Newton lsmr steps on active inequalities plus LP stress reweighting and final trust-region LP polish.
direction: Implement a target-cosine homotopy with active-set SQP and stress testing rather than minimising the smoothed maximum directly: starting from `best.npy`, attempt targets $c=\max\cos-10^{-6},-2\times10^{-6},-5\times10^{-6}$ in succession; maintain all pairs above $c-3\times10^{-4}$ as active inequalities, project their Jacobians onto the tangent spaces, and use damped Gauss–Newton/`scipy.sparse.linalg.lsmr` steps with trust radii $10^{-2}\to10^{-4}$ to minimise squared positive violations. After each near-feasible step solve an LP for weights $w_{ij}\ge0$ on active pairs minimising each point's tangent imbalance $\|\sum_j w_{ij}(x_j-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle x_i)\|$, drop persistently zero/negative-stress contacts, recruit newly tight pairs, and continue only while feasibility improves; finish with the existing trust-region LP and return the incumbent if no target is reached. This directly searches for a lower configuration with a recruited, stress-balanced contact set instead of accepting whatever contacts LP tolerance happens to leave behind.

idea: Search block-diagonal cyclic orbit codes with few seed degrees of freedom over all orbit sizes dividing 168, race many coprime frequency quadruples with seed-only row-normalised softmax Adam, then break symmetry with two noise scales and re-jam with full-dimensional quench plus trust-region LP polish.
direction: Search symmetry-generated codes with very few degrees of freedom, then break the symmetry: for orbit sizes $m\in\{84,56,42,28,24,21\}$ with respectively $2,3,4,6,7,8$ seed points, construct block-diagonal rotations in four coordinate planes with angles $2\pi(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)/m$ for random integer frequency quadruples coprime to $m$, generate all $m$ rotations of each seed, and optimise only the seeds with row-normalised softmax Adam ($\beta:30\to600$) under the exact 168-point max-cosine objective. Enumerate many frequency/seed combinations with short races, fully quench and LP-polish the best few after adding symmetry-breaking noise of sizes $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-2}$, and retain results whose contact-degree histogram differs from the incumbent. Such orbit codes automatically distribute contacts evenly across all points and may land in a balanced basin inaccessible by perturbing the asymmetric record.

idea: Large cap surgery removing 10/16/24 co-aligned points and jointly re-optimizing the whole cap against frozen remainder plus itself before global re-jam to force topology changes.
direction: Perform large spatial-cluster surgery at fixed $N=168$: choose either a highly contacted hub or a random direction, remove the $k\in\{10,16,24\}$ points most aligned with it (not merely individual rattlers), freeze the remainder, and simultaneously reinsert the removed points by first selecting mutually distant candidates from 20,000 random probes plus refined holes and then jointly optimising the inserted block against both frozen points and itself with a high-$\beta$ soft-min objective. Unfreeze everything for a balanced quench, hard-max polish, and short LP; accept moves by post-polish score with occasional simulated-annealing acceptance within $2\times10^{-6}$ of the best, but reject configurations whose degree sequence at a $10^{-4}$ contact threshold matches an archived basin. Iterating whole-cap removal changes contact topology collectively, whereas previous one-point void relocation preserves the surrounding jam.

direction: Use a particle-number ladder as the global path: remove 24–40 points from the incumbent, or start from an optimised 128–144-point subset/random code where the attainable cosine is less constrained, then regrow to 168 by repeatedly inserting the globally refined deepest hole and fully re-optimising after every one to four insertions with annealed softmax Adam followed by LP. Because contacts are recruited gradually while slack is still large, the final contact network can reorganise globally rather than inheriting the record's overloaded near-contact ordering.

Optimize only the reduced variables with row-normalized softmax Adam, using several random and E8-derived seeds, then release first the orbit phases or antipodal pairing and finally all coordinates, with a short full-dimensional quench after each release. Rank candidates before the final LP not just by maximum cosine but also by contact-degree balance, since the desired symmetric basin should have repeated contact patterns distributed over all orbits. Guard every construction with exception handling and a preloaded fallback from `best.npy`, reserving the last 30 seconds for LP polishing so that a failed symmetric experiment cannot cause a harness failure.

idea: Target-cosine homotopy with active-set damped Gauss-Newton lsmr steps and stress-balanced pruning followed by trust-region LP squeeze.
direction: Implement a target-cosine homotopy with active-set SQP and stress testing rather than minimising the smoothed maximum directly: starting from `best.npy`, attempt targets $c=\max\cos-10^{-6},-2\times10^{-6},-5\times10^{-6}$ in succession; maintain all pairs above $c-3\times10^{-4}$ as active inequalities, project their Jacobians onto the tangent spaces, and use damped Gauss–Newton/`scipy.sparse.linalg.lsmr` steps with trust radii $10^{-2}\to10^{-4}$ to minimise squared positive violations. After each near-feasible step solve an LP for weights $w_{ij}\ge0$ on active pairs minimising each point's tangent imbalance $\|\sum_j w_{ij}(x_j-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle x_i)\|$, drop persistently zero/negative-stress contacts, recruit newly tight pairs, and continue only while feasibility improves; finish with the existing trust-region LP and return the incumbent if no target is reached. This directly searches for a lower configuration with a recruited, stress-balanced contact set instead of accepting whatever contacts LP tolerance happens to leave behind.

idea: Eject overloaded hubs into refined spherical holes and re-jam with balanced global-plus-local softmax Adam to reach a new isostatic basin, finished by trust-region LP squeeze.
Escape the unbalanced 10-hub basin with void-surgery ejection of overloaded points plus balanced global-local softmax re-jamming from perturbed and random starts finished by trust-region LP squeeze.
Degree-targeted core surgery replacing dense near-contact clusters with softmax-refined void probes then balanced global-plus-local anneal and LP squeeze.
direction: Perform degree-targeted core surgery rather than relocating only rattlers. Build the near-contact graph at slack $2\times10^{-4}$, identify the 12–24 points with the largest weighted degree or belonging to the densest mutually connected cluster, and remove them; generate at least 20000 random probes, refine the best mutually separated probes against the remaining points by softmax hole-minimization, and insert replacements into the largest spherical voids. Re-jam the modified code with a balanced global-plus-per-point softmax anneal ($\beta$ increasing from about 30 to 300, Adam learning rate decaying from $10^{-2}$ to $10^{-4}$), followed by LP polishing, but judge intermediate basins not by score alone: accept a slightly worse score, up to $2\times10^{-4}$ above the incumbent, if it substantially improves balance metrics such as minimum near-contact degree, degree entropy, or the fraction of points with $m_i$ within $10^{-4}$ of $M$. Repeat this surgery with several cluster sizes and random seeds under strict time checks, always retaining the best fully polished configuration as the safe return value.

idea: Stress-recruiting Adam with variance plus slack penalties and equilibrium-stress reweighting, followed by violation homotopy and wide LP squeeze.
direction: Implement stress- and contact-recruiting optimization instead of minimizing only the global maximum. Starting from `best.npy`, define $m_i=\max_{j\ne i}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle$ and optimize, by tangent-space Adam for about 60 seconds, a loss combining a high-$\beta$ log-sum-exp over all pair cosines with penalties for the variance of $m_i$ and for points satisfying $m_i<M-10^{-4}$, thereby forcing currently slack points to acquire near-contacts while lowering the global maximum. Every 500 steps, construct the graph using pairs with slack below $10^{-4}$, estimate nonnegative equilibrium-stress weights by exponentiated-gradient minimization of the squared tangent residual, delete persistently zero-weight constraints, and reweight each point’s softmax gradient inversely to its weighted contact degree. Then run targets $c=M-10^{-5}, M-3\times10^{-5}, M-10^{-4}$ in a feasibility homotopy using $\sum \mathrm{relu}(g_{ij}-c)^2$, accepting a lower target only when violation reaches zero, and finish with the established trust-region LP using a wide active set of up to 4000 pairs. Keep the best feasible configuration encountered and return it if any stage fails.

idea: Break the unbalanced basin with perturbed balanced soft-max quenches plus hub ejection into deepest spherical holes, then re-jam and squeeze with trust-region LP.
